The period over which unpaid community work
must be performed, that a court specifies in a fines
work order, must not be such a period as would
require an offender to perform more than 20 hours
of unpaid community work in any 7 day period.

Despite subsection (2) an offender may perform
unpaid community work for up to 40 hours in a
period of 7 days if he or she requests to do so and
signs a written consent to performing the extra
number of hours.

nodes.heading: Cumulative unpaid community work if there are several orders

history.raw: S. 69R inserted by No. 32/2013 s. 47 (as amended by No. 77/2013 ss 45, 48).

nodes.text:
The number of hours of unpaid community work
required to be performed by an offender under a
fines work order must, unless otherwise directed
by a court, be performed cumulatively on any
hours of unpaid community work required to be
performed under another fines work order that is
in force in respect of the offender, whether the
other fines work order is made before or at the
same time as the first mentioned order.

A court must not give a direction under this
section that is not consistent with section 69Q.

nodes.heading: Terms and operation of fines work orders

history.raw: Pt 3 Div. 7 (Heading) substituted as Pt 3B Div. 4 (Heading) by No. 65/2011 s. 41, renumbered as Pt 3BA Div. 3 by No. 26/2012 s. 60.
Pt 3 Div. 7 (Heading and s. 83A) inserted by No. 19/1999 s. 9.

nodes.heading: Period of a fines work order

history.raw: S. 69S inserted by No. 32/2013 s. 47 (as amended by No. 77/2013 ss 45, 48).

nodes.text:
The period of a fines work order is the period
determined by the court in accordance with
section 69Q.

Subject to subsection (3), the court must fix the
date on which a fines work order commences,
which must not be more than 3 months after the
order is made.

If, under section 69R, the hours of unpaid
community work required to be performed by an
offender under a fines work order are to be
performed cumulatively on any hours of unpaid
community work required to be performed under
another fines work order, the later fines work
order commences on the completion of the earlier
order.

nodes.heading: When does a fines work order expire?
nodes.text:
A fines work order expires on the satisfactory
completion of the hours of work that the court
ordered that the offender must perform.

history.raw: S. 69T inserted by No. 32/2013 s. 47 (as amended by No. 77/2013 ss 45, 48).

nodes.heading: Part payment of fine to reduce unpaid community work

history.raw: S. 69U inserted by No. 32/2013 s. 47 (as amended by No. 77/2013 ss 45, 48).

nodes.text:
This section applies if at any time while a fines
work order is in force part of the amount then
remaining unpaid is paid as required in
subsection (3).

The number of hours of work which the person is
required to perform must be reduced by the
number of hours bearing as nearly as possible the
same proportion to the total number of hours as
the amount paid bears to the whole amount in
respect of which the order was made.

An amount being paid as referred to in
subsection (1) must be paid, in accordance with
the regulations, to the Secretary by or on behalf of
the person required to perform unpaid community
work.

nodes.heading: Terms of a fines work order

history.raw: S. 69V inserted by No. 32/2013 s. 47 (as amended by No. 77/2013 ss 45, 48).

nodes.text:
The following terms are attached to each fines
work order—

the offender must not commit (whether in or
outside Victoria) during the period of the
order, an offence punishable by
imprisonment;

the offender must report to the community
corrections centre specified in the order
within 2 clear working days after the order
comes into force;

the offender must comply with any direction
given by the Secretary that is necessary for
the Secretary to give to ensure that the
offender complies with the order.

A direction may be given by the Secretary under
subsection (1)(g) either orally or in writing.

history.raw: S. 69W inserted by No. 32/2013 s. 47 (as amended by No. 77/2013 ss 45, 48).

nodes.text:
The Secretary may suspend the operation of a
fines work order or any condition of that order for
a period.

The Secretary may suspend an order or any
condition of the order under subsection (1)—
if the offender is ill; or
in other exceptional circumstances.

If the Secretary suspends the operation of an order
or a condition of an order under subsection (1),
the period of the suspension does not count in
calculating the period for which the order is to
remain in force.

nodes.heading: Secretary may direct offender to report at another place or to another person

history.raw: S. 69X inserted by No. 32/2013 s. 47 (as amended by No. 77/2013 ss 45, 48).

nodes.text:
If, because an offender has changed his or her
place of residence or for any other reason it is not
convenient that the offender should report at a
place or to a person specified in a fines work
order, the Secretary may direct the offender to
report at another place or to another person.

An offender must report as directed under
subsection (1) as if that place or person had been
specified in the order.

nodes.heading: Enforcement of fines against bodies corporate
Enforcement of fines against bodies corporate

history.raw: S. 69Y inserted by No. 32/2013 s. 47 (as amended by No. 77/2013 ss 45, 48).

nodes.text:
If a body corporate defaults in respect of a fine or
of any instalment under an instalment order by not
making payment by the end of 28 days after the
due date for payment the court or the proper
officer may issue a warrant to seize property
against it.

The court or proper officer must not issue a
warrant under subsection (1) in respect of a
registered court fine within the meaning of the
Fines Reform Act 2014.

nodes.heading: Notice of orders to be given
nodes.text:
An order under this Part is not binding on an
offender if the offender has not been given notice
of it in the manner required by or under this Part.

history.raw: S. 69Z inserted by No. 32/2013 s. 47 (as amended by No. 77/2013 ss 45, 48).

nodes.heading: Oath or affirmation
nodes.text:
A court, or a proper officer of a court, may
administer an oath or affirmation for the purposes
of proceedings under this Part.

history.raw: S. 69ZA inserted by No. 32/2013 s. 47 (as amended by No. 77/2013 ss 45, 48).

nodes.heading: Application of fines etc.
nodes.text:
The whole or any part of a fine, penalty or sum of
money which by or under any Act is authorised or
directed to be imposed on a person forms part of,
and must be paid into, the Consolidated Fund if no
other way of appropriating or applying it is
prescribed by law.

history.raw: S. 69ZB inserted by No. 32/2013 s. 47 (as amended by No. 77/2013 ss 45, 48).

nodes.heading: Penalty payable to body corporate
nodes.text:
A forfeiture or penalty payable to a party
aggrieved under an Act relating to an offence
(whether indictable or summary) is payable to a
body corporate if it is the party aggrieved.

history.raw: S. 69ZC inserted by No. 32/2013 s. 47 (as amended by No. 77/2013 ss 45, 48).

nodes.heading: Recovery of penalties
nodes.text:
If an Act or a subordinate instrument—
then, unless the contrary intention appears, the
penalty must be recovered only before the
Magistrates' Court.

history.raw: S. 69ZD inserted by No. 32/2013 s. 47 (as amended by No. 77/2013 ss 45, 48).

nodes.text:
provides for a penalty to be recovered from
any person—
summarily; or
on summary conviction; or
before the Magistrates' Court; or

uses any other words that imply that a
penalty is to be recovered before the
Magistrates' Court; or

does not provide a form or mode of
procedure for the recovery of a penalty—

nodes.heading: Order made by Court of Appeal
nodes.text:
For the purposes of any proceeding under this Part
or Division 2 of Part 3C—

history.raw: S. 69ZE inserted by No. 32/2013 s. 47 (as amended by No. 77/2013 ss 45, 48).

nodes.text:
a fine or a time to pay order or an instalment
order or a fines work order made by the
Court of Appeal on an appeal must be taken
to have been made by the court from whose
decision the appeal was brought; and

the provisions about proceedings under this
Part or Division 2 of Part 3C apply as if the
court from which the appeal was made were
the sentencing court.

nodes.heading: Rules of court
nodes.text:
The power to make rules under the Supreme
Court Act 1986, the County Court Act 1958 and
the Magistrates' Court Act 1989 extends to and
applies in relation to the making of rules for or
with respect to—

history.raw: S. 69ZF inserted by No. 32/2013 s. 47 (as amended by No. 77/2013 ss 45, 48).

nodes.text:
the manner of making applications under
section 65; or

court procedure and the procedure of the
proper officer under this Part; or

securing the attendance of an offender before
the court and the production of documents by
an offender to the court if the offender
defaults in the payment of a fine or of an
instalment under an instalment order and
empowering the issue of a summons or
warrant to arrest or the making of an order
for that purpose; or

the issue and execution under this Part of
summonses, warrants to arrest, warrants of
execution and warrants to imprison; or

the functions of the proper officer of the
court under this Part; or

the costs of proceedings if an order is made
under section 69L; or
the forms for the purposes of this Part; or

the manner of service or filing of any
documents under this Part; or

any other matter or thing required or
permitted by this Part or necessary to give
effect to this Part.

nodes.heading: Application to infringement enforcement procedure
nodes.text:
This Part does not apply to the use of the
procedures for the enforcement of infringement
penalties under the Fines Reform Act 2014.

history.raw: S. 69ZG inserted by No. 32/2013 s. 47 (as amended by No. 77/2013 ss 45, 48), amended by No. 47/2014 s. 312.

nodes.heading: Purpose of orders under this Division

nodes.text: An order may be made under this Division—

to take account of the trivial, technical or
minor nature of the offence committed;

to allow for circumstances in which it is
inappropriate to record a conviction;

to allow for the existence of other
extenuating or exceptional circumstances
that justify the court showing mercy to an
offender.

For the purpose of any proceedings under
Subdivision (4), an order made under this
Division on appeal by the Court of Appeal must
be taken to have been made by the court from
whose decision the appeal was brought.

nodes.heading: Abolition of common law bonds
nodes.text:
A court does not have jurisdiction to release a
convicted offender on a recognisance or bond to
be of good behaviour and to appear for sentence
when called on.

nodes.heading: Limitation on making of orders under this Division
nodes.text:
The power of a court to make an order under this
Division in respect of an offence is subject to any
specific provision relating to the offence.

nodes.heading: Subdivision (2)—Release on conviction
nodes.text: Subdivision (2)—Release on conviction

A court, on convicting a person of an offence,
may adjourn the proceeding for a period of up to
5 years and release the offender on the offender
giving an undertaking with conditions attached.

An undertaking under subsection (1) must have as
conditions—

that the offender attends before the court if
called on to do so during the period of the
adjournment and, if the court so specifies, at
the time to which the further hearing is
adjourned; and

history.raw: S. 72(2)(a) amended by No. 68/2009 s. 97(Sch. item 110.49).

nodes.text:
that the offender is of good behaviour during
the period of the adjournment; and

that the offender observes any conditions
attached by the court and may include a
condition requiring the offender to make a
payment to an organisation that provides a
charitable or community service or to the
court for payment to such an organisation.

Subject to Division 2 of Part 3BA, a court may
attach a justice plan condition that the offender
participate in the services specified in a justice
plan for a period of up to 2 years specified by the
court or the period of the adjournment, whichever
is the shorter.

An offender who has given an undertaking under
subsection (1) may be called on to attend before
the court—

history.raw: S. 72(4) amended by No. 68/2009 s. 97(Sch. item 110.50).

nodes.text: by order of the court; or

by notice issued by the proper officer of the
court.

An order or notice under subsection (4) must be
served on the offender not less than 4 days before
the time specified in it for the attendance.

history.raw: S. 72(5) amended by No. 68/2009 s. 97(Sch. item 110.51).

nodes.text:
If at the time to which the further hearing of a
proceeding is adjourned the court is satisfied that
the offender has observed the conditions of the
undertaking, it must discharge the offender
without any further hearing of the proceeding.

nodes.heading: Unconditional discharge
nodes.text:
A court may discharge a person whom it has
convicted of an offence.

nodes.heading: Compensation or restitution
nodes.text:
A court may make an order for compensation or
restitution in addition to making an order under
this Subdivision.

nodes.heading: Subdivision (3)—Release without conviction
nodes.text: Subdivision (3)—Release without conviction

A court, on being satisfied that a person is guilty
of an offence, may (without recording a
conviction) adjourn the proceeding for a period of
up to 60 months and release the offender on the
offender giving an undertaking with conditions
attached.

An undertaking under subsection (1) must have as
conditions—

that the offender attends before the court if
called on to do so during the period of the
adjournment and, if the court so specifies, at
the time to which the further hearing is
adjourned; and

history.raw: S. 75(2)(a) amended by No. 68/2009 s. 97(Sch. item 110.52).

nodes.text:
that the offender is of good behaviour during
the period of the adjournment; and

that the offender observes any special
conditions imposed by the court and may
include a condition requiring the offender to
make a payment to an organisation that
provides a charitable or community service
or to the court for payment to such an
organisation.

Subject to Division 2 of Part 3BA, a court may
attach a justice plan condition that the offender
participate in the services specified in a justice
plan for a period of up to 2 years specified by the
court or the period of the adjournment, whichever
is the shorter.

An offender who has given an undertaking under
subsection (1) may be called on to attend before
the court—

history.raw: S. 75(4) amended by No. 68/2009 s. 97(Sch. item 110.53).

nodes.text: by order of the court; or

by notice issued by the proper officer of the
court.

An order or notice under subsection (4) must be
served on the offender not less than 4 days before
the time specified in it for the attendance.

history.raw: S. 75(5) amended by No. 68/2009 s. 97(Sch. item 110.54).

nodes.text:
If at the time to which the further hearing of a
proceeding is adjourned the court is satisfied that
the offender has observed the conditions of the
undertaking, it must dismiss the charge without
any further hearing of the proceeding.

nodes.heading: Unconditional dismissal
nodes.text:
A court, on being satisfied that a person is guilty
of an offence, may (without recording a
conviction) dismiss the charge.

nodes.heading: Compensation or restitution
nodes.text:
A court may make an order for compensation or
restitution in addition to making an order under
this Subdivision.

nodes.heading: Subdivision (4)—Variation of orders for release
nodes.text: Subdivision (4)—Variation of orders for release

nodes.heading: on adjournment
nodes.text: on adjournment

nodes.heading: Variation of order for release on adjournment

nodes.text:
A court which has under Subdivision (2) or (3)
made an order for the release of an offender on an
adjournment (with or without recording a
conviction) may, on application under this
subsection, if satisfied—
vary the order or cancel it and, subject to
subsection (2), deal with the offender for the
offence or offences with respect to which it was
made in any manner in which the court could deal
with the offender if it had just found the offender
guilty of that offence or those offences.

that the circumstances of the offender have
materially altered since the order was made
and as a result the offender will not be able
to comply with any condition of the
undertaking; or

that the circumstances of the offender were
wrongly stated or were not accurately
presented to the court or the author of a
pre-sentence report before the order was
made; or

that the offender is no longer willing to
comply with the conditions of the
undertaking—

A court, in determining how to deal with an
offender under subsection (1) must take into
account the extent to which the offender has
complied with the order.

An application under subsection (1) may be made
at any time while the order is in force by—
the offender; or

a prescribed person, or a member of a
prescribed class of persons; or
the Director of Public Prosecutions.

Notice of an application under subsection (1) must
be given—
to the offender; and

to the Director of Public Prosecutions (if the
sentencing court was the Supreme Court or
the County Court) or to the informant or
police prosecutor (if the sentencing court
was the Magistrates' Court).

The court may order that a warrant to arrest be
issued against the offender if he or she does not
attend before the court on the hearing of the
application.

A court that is considering—
may attach a condition to the order directing that
the offender participate in the services specified in
the plan prepared under subsection (3)(c).
making a community correction order; or

releasing an offender on adjournment with or
without recording a conviction—

In attaching a condition under subsection (1) the
court must—

consider the plan and the other information
requested under subsection (3); and

have regard to those objectives and
principles specified in Part 2 of the
Disability Act 2006.

A court which is considering making an order
attaching a justice plan condition may request—

a pre-sentence report under Division 1A of
Part 3; and

a statement from the Secretary to the
Department of Health and Human Services
that the person has an intellectual disability
within the meaning of the Disability
Act 2006; and

a plan of available services designed to
reduce the likelihood of the offender
committing further offences and that is in
accordance with the objectives and principles
of Part 2 of the Disability Act 2006.

When attaching a justice plan condition, the
condition may apply for a period of up to 2 years,
as specified by the court or the period of the
sentence (whichever is the shorter).

If a court attaches a justice plan condition it must
cause a copy of the order to be supplied to the
Secretary to the Department of Health and Human
Services.

nodes.heading: Review of justice plan by Secretary

nodes.text:
The Secretary to the Department of Human
Services must review a justice plan—
until the condition of the sentence ceases to have
effect.

not later than one year after the imposing of
the order to which the justice plan condition
is attached under section 80 and thereafter at
intervals not exceeding one year; or

as directed by the court at the time of
sentencing—

history.raw: S. 81(2)(b) amended by No. 45/1996 s. 18(Sch. 2 item 11.12), substituted by No. 65/2011 s. 36(5).

nodes.text:
The Secretary to the Department of Human
Services may review a justice plan if an
application is made to him or her to do so by—
the offender; or

if the sentence is a community correction
order, the Secretary; or

if the sentence is a an order under
Subdivision (2) or (3) of Division 2, a
prescribed person or a member of a
prescribed class of persons.

nodes.heading: Review of justice plan condition by sentencing court

nodes.text:
If on an application under this subsection the court
which attached a justice plan condition to an order
under section 80(1) is satisfied—
it may confirm, vary or cancel the condition.

that the offender is no longer willing to
comply with the condition; or

that the needs of the offender are not being
met by the condition; or

that the offender has failed without
reasonable excuse to comply with the
condition; or
that the condition is no longer appropriate—

history.raw: S. 82(2)(d) amended by No. 46/1998 s. 7(Sch. 1), substituted by No. 23/2006 s. 228(2), amended by No. 65/2011 s. 38(4)(c).

nodes.text:
An application under subsection (1) may be made
at any time while the justice plan condition is in
force by—
the offender; or

if the sentence is a community correction
order, the Secretary; or

if the sentence is an order under
Subdivision (2) or (3) of Division 2, a
prescribed person or a member of a
prescribed class of persons; or

the Secretary to the Department of Human
Services.

Notice of an application under subsection (1) must
be given—
to the offender; and

to the Director of Public Prosecutions (if the
sentencing court was the Supreme Court or
the County Court) or to the informant or
police prosecutor (if the sentencing court
was the Magistrates' Court).

The court may order that a warrant to arrest be
issued against the offender if he or she does not
attend before the court on the hearing of the
application.

If the court cancels the justice plan condition, it
may cancel the sentence and, subject to
subsection (6), deal with the offender for the
offence or offences with respect to which the
sentence was imposed in any manner in which the
court could deal with the offender if it had just
found the offender guilty of that offence or those
offences.

In determining how to deal with an offender
following the cancellation by it of a sentence, a
court must take into account the extent to which
the offender had complied with the sentence
before its cancellation.

A court may make an order directing that the
offender be detained for a period of up to 5 years
in a specified residential treatment facility to
receive specified treatment if—

the offender has been found guilty of a
serious offence within the meaning of the
definition of serious offence in section 3(1);
or

the offender has been found guilty of an
offence against section 40(1) (sexual
assault), or section 41(1) (sexual assault by
compelling sexual touching), of the Crimes
Act 1958.

If a court is considering making a residential
treatment order the court may request—

a pre-sentence report in accordance with
Division 1A of Part 3; and

a statement from the Secretary to the
Department of Health and Human Services
that the person has an intellectual disability
within the meaning of the Disability
Act 2006; and
a plan of available services.

A court may only make a residential treatment
order if the Secretary to the Department of Health
and Human Services has specified—

that the person is suitable for admission to a
residential treatment facility; and

in the plan of available services, that services
are available in a residential treatment
facility.

If a court makes a residential treatment order it
must cause a copy of the order to be supplied to
the Secretary to the Department of Health and
Human Services.

nodes.heading: Review of residential treatment order by sentencing court

nodes.text:
If on an application under this subsection the court
which imposed a residential treatment order under
section 82AA is satisfied—
it may confirm, vary or cancel the residential
treatment order.

that the offender is not complying with the
residential treatment order; or

that the needs of the offender are not being
met by the residential treatment order; or

that the residential treatment order is no
longer appropriate—

An application under subsection (1) may be made
at any time while the residential treatment order is
in force by—
the offender; or
the Secretary; or

the Secretary to the Department of Human
Services.

Notice of an application under subsection (1) must
be given—
to the offender; and

to the Director of Public Prosecutions (if the
sentencing court was the Supreme Court or
the County Court) or to the informant or
police prosecutor (if the sentencing court
was the Magistrates' Court).

The court may order that a warrant to arrest be
issued against the offender if he or she does not
attend before the court on the hearing of the
application.

If the court cancels the residential treatment order,
it may cancel the sentence and, subject to
subsection (6), deal with the offender for the
offence or offences with respect to which the
sentence was imposed in any manner in which the
court could deal with the offender if it had just
found the offender guilty of that offence or those
offences.

In determining how to deal with an offender
following the cancellation by it of a sentence, a
court must take into account the extent to which
the offender had complied with the sentence
before its cancellation.

nodes.heading: Notice of application
nodes.text:
Notice of an application under section 82(1)
or 82A(1) must be given to an offender by—

not less than 14 days before the date of
hearing of the application posting a true copy
of the application addressed to the offender
at his or her last known place of residence or
business; or

not less than 5 days before the date of
hearing of the application—

delivering to the offender personally a
true copy of the application; or

leaving a true copy of the application
for the offender at his or her last known
place of residence or business with a
person who apparently resides or works
there and who apparently is not less
than 16 years old.

nodes.heading: Deferral of sentencing in the Magistrates' Court or County Court

nodes.text:
If the Magistrates' Court or County Court finds a
person guilty of an offence and—
the court may defer sentencing the offender for a
period not exceeding 12 months.

the court is of the opinion that sentencing
should, in the interests of the offender, be
deferred; and

the offender agrees to a deferral of
sentencing—

The court may defer sentencing the offender under
subsection (1) for any one or more of the
following purposes—

to allow the offender's capacity for and
prospects of rehabilitation to be assessed;

history.raw: S. 83A(1)(a) amended by No. 72/2004 s. 39, repealed by No. 77/2010 s. 21(1)(b).

nodes.text:
to allow the offender to demonstrate that
rehabilitation has taken place;

for any other purpose that the court considers
appropriate having regard to the offender and
the circumstances of the case.

In making an order deferring a sentence under
subsection (1), the court may determine the date at
which the offender must re-appear before the
court for a review of the order.

Dates fixed under subsection (1B) must be
between the date on which the order deferring the
sentence is made and the date to which the
proceeding has been adjourned.

On the review of an order deferring a sentence
under this section, the court may—
take no further action; or

cancel the order deferring the sentence and
proceed to sentence the offender, as if the
matter were an adjourned hearing to which
subsection (3) applies.

In making an order deferring a sentence under
subsection (1), the court may order that any
review of the order under subsection (1B) be dealt
with by the court constituted by the person who
made the order deferring the sentence.

If the Magistrates' Court or County Court defers
sentencing an offender, it—

must adjourn the proceeding for a period of
up to 12 months; and

may release the offender on his or her
undertaking to attend before the court on the
date fixed for sentence or release the
offender on bail or extend his or her bail to
that date; and

may order a pre-sentence report in respect of
the offender.

On the adjourned hearing, the court must, in
determining the appropriate sentence for an
offender, have regard to—

the offender's behaviour during the period of
deferral; and

subject to section 8D, any pre-sentence
report ordered under subsection (2)(c); and
any other relevant matter.

If an offender is found guilty of an offence during
a period of deferral under this section, the court
may—

re-list the adjourned proceeding on a day
earlier than the day to which it was
adjourned under subsection (2)(a); and

on the adjourned hearing make any order that
the court could have made if it had not
deferred sentencing.

The court may order that a warrant to arrest be
issued against the offender if he or she does not
attend before the court on the adjourned hearing.

Nothing in this section removes any requirement
imposed on the Magistrates' Court or County
Court by or under this or any other Act to impose
any disqualification on, or make any other order in
respect of, a person found guilty or convicted of
an offence, including an order cancelling or
suspending a driver licence or permit or
disqualifying the offender from obtaining one for
any period.

history.raw: Pt 3C (Heading and ss 83AB– 83AT) inserted by No. 65/2011 s. 43.

nodes.heading: Contravention of order for release on adjournment
nodes.text:
An offender who is subject to an order under
section 72 or 75 for release on the adjournment of
the proceeding must not contravene that order,
unless the offender has a reasonable excuse.
Penalty: Level 10 fine.

An offender who is subject to a community
correction order must not contravene that order,
unless the offender has a reasonable excuse.
Penalty: 3 months imprisonment.

A proceeding is not able to be brought against a
person for an offence under subsection (1) in
relation to conduct of that person in respect of
which that person has been acquitted, convicted or
found guilty of an offence under section 83AE
or 83AF.

nodes.heading: Contravention of fine conversion order
nodes.text:
An offender who is subject to a fine conversion
order must not contravene that order unless the
offender has a reasonable excuse.
Penalty: Level 10 fine.

nodes.heading: Contravention of fine default unpaid community work order
nodes.text:
An offender who is subject to a fine default
unpaid community work order must not
contravene that order unless the offender has a
reasonable excuse.
Penalty: Level 10 fine.

nodes.heading: Particular contraventions of directions of Secretary

nodes.text:
An offender who is subject to a community
correction order and who is attending at a place
under a direction given by the Secretary in
compliance with section 45(1)(f), must not leave
that place unless—
Penalty: Level 11 fine.

the offender has first obtained the permission
of the Secretary; or
the offender has a reasonable excuse.

An offender who is subject to a community
correction order and who is required to attend at a
place under a direction given by the Secretary in
compliance with section 45(1)(f), must, unless the
offender has a reasonable excuse, notify the
Secretary if he or she is unable to attend as
required—
Penalty: Level 11 fine.

at least 24 hours before the offender is due to
attend the location if the offender has at least
24 hours notice of that inability; or

immediately on becoming unable to attend if
the offender did not have at least 24 hours
notice of his or her inability to attend at the
location.

An offender who is subject to a community
correction order and who is required to attend at a
place under a direction given by the Secretary in
compliance with section 45(1)(f), must attend at
the place on the required day and time unless—
Penalty: Level 11 fine.

the offender has obtained the permission of
the Secretary not to attend; or
the offender has a reasonable excuse.

An offender who is subject to a community
correction order and who is required to attend at a
place under a direction given by the Secretary in
compliance with section 45(1)(f) must produce a
medical certificate, as soon as is practicable, if the
offender has not attended because of illness.
Penalty: Level 11 fine.

An offender who is subject to a community
correction order who is required to attend at a
community corrections centre under the order
must not enter an unauthorised area of the
community corrections centre without the
permission of the Secretary.
Penalty: Level 11 fine.

In this section—
unauthorised area means an area designated by
the Secretary to be an unauthorised area.

A proceeding is not able to be brought against a
person for an offence under this section in relation
to conduct of that person in respect of which that
person has been acquitted, convicted or found
guilty of an offence under section 83AD or 83AF.

nodes.heading: Offence to fail to obey a written direction of Secretary

nodes.text:
An offender who is subject to a community
correction order must not contravene a written
direction of the Secretary that is given under
section 46 unless that person has a reasonable
excuse.
Penalty: Level 11 fine.

A proceeding is not able to be brought against a
person for an offence under subsection (1) in
relation to conduct of that person in respect of
which that person has been acquitted, convicted or
found guilty of an offence under section 83AD
or 83AE.

history.raw: S. 83AG inserted by No. 65/2011 s. 43, substituted by No. 26/2012 s. 62.

nodes.text:
A proceeding for an offence under section 83AC,
83AD, 83ADA, 83ADB, 83AE or 83AF is
commenced by filing a charge-sheet in the
Magistrates' Court.

A charge-sheet must be filed under subsection (1)
by—
as the case requires.
the Director of Public Prosecutions; or

a crown prosecutor within the meaning of the
Criminal Procedure Act 2009; or

a member of staff of the Office of Public
Prosecutions who is a lawyer; or
a police officer; or

history.raw: S. 83AG(2)(d) amended by No. 37/2014 s. 10(Sch. item 151.3).

nodes.text:
an informant in the proceeding for which the
sentencing order was made that is the subject
of the charge; or
a prescribed person; or
a member of a prescribed class of person; or
the Secretary—

Subject to this Act, a proceeding commenced
under this Division is to be in accordance with the
provisions of and regulations and rules made
under—
with any necessary modifications, and in
particular with the modification that a reference to
a person accused of an offence or an accused
person, is taken to be a reference to the offender.
the Criminal Procedure Act 2009;
the Bail Act 1977;
the Magistrates' Court Act 1989—

In particular, without limiting subsection (3),
section 12 of the Criminal Procedure Act 2009
applies to a proceeding commenced under this
section with the modification that a reference to
section 6 is taken to be a reference to
section 83AG of this Act.

history.raw: S. 83AH inserted by No. 65/2011 s. 43, substituted by No. 26/2012 s. 62.

nodes.text:
A proceeding for an offence under section 83AC,
83AD, 83ADA or 83ADB must be commenced—

if the contravention is constituted by the
offender committing another offence
punishable by imprisonment while the order
is in force, within 6 months after the person
is convicted or found guilty of the later
offence, subject to subsection (2); or

if the contravention is not constituted by the
offender committing another offence
punishable by imprisonment while the order
is in force, within 1 year after the order
ceases to be in force.

A proceeding for an offence under section 83AC,
83AD, 83ADA or 83ADB to which
subsection (1)(a) applies must not be commenced
more than 2 years after the order ceases to be in
force.

The time limit for the commencement of a proceeding for a
summary offence under section 7 of the Criminal
Procedure Act 2009 applies to an offence against
section 83AE or 83AF.

nodes.heading: Issue of summons or warrant to arrest

history.raw: S. 83AI inserted by No. 65/2011 s. 43, substituted by No. 26/2012 s. 62.

nodes.text:
A summons issued for the purposes of a
proceeding commenced under section 83AG for
an offence under section 83AC, 83AD, 83ADA
or 83ADB must direct the offender to attend to
answer to the charge—

at the proper venue of the Magistrates' Court,
if the order that is the subject of the offence
was made by the Magistrates' Court; or

at the Supreme Court or the County Court, if
the order that is the subject of the offence
was made by either court.

A warrant to arrest issued for the purposes of a
proceeding commenced under section 83AG for
an offence under section 83AC, 83AD, 83ADA
or 83ADB must—

be issued in accordance with Part 4 of the
Magistrates' Court Act 1989; and

authorise the person to whom it is directed to
bring the offender when arrested before a
bail justice or the sentencing court to be dealt
with according to law.

history.raw: S. 83AJ inserted by No. 65/2011 s. 43, substituted by No. 26/2012 s. 62.

nodes.text:
If a proceeding is commenced under
section 83AG for an offence under section 83AC,
83AD, 83ADA or 83ADB, and the Magistrates'
Court did not make the order that is the subject of
the offence, the Magistrates' Court must order that
the proceeding be transferred to the appropriate
venue of the sentencing court.

An order made under subsection (1) that transfers
a proceeding takes effect—

if a summons has been issued under
section 83AI(1) on the filing of the evidence
of service of the summons in the sentencing
court; or

if a warrant to arrest has been issued under
section 83AI(2) on the execution of the
warrant against the offender.

The Magistrates' Court under subsection (1) may
be constituted by a proper officer of the court.

If a proceeding is transferred to the Supreme
Court or the County Court under subsection (1) it
may be heard and determined without a jury and
in accordance with Chapter 3 of the Criminal
Procedure Act 2009 subject to any modifications
as set out in the rules of the court.

nodes.heading: Issue of warrant to arrest on failure to comply with bail or summons
nodes.text:
If a proceeding is transferred under section 83AJ
and an offender does not attend before the
sentencing court—
the sentencing court may issue a warrant to arrest
the offender.

history.raw: S. 83AK inserted by No. 65/2011 s. 43, substituted by No. 26/2012 s. 62.

nodes.text:
in accordance with his or her undertaking of
bail; or

in answer to a summons which has been
served—

nodes.heading: Process where offender before higher court, orders of that court

history.raw: S. 83AL inserted by No. 65/2011 s. 43, substituted by No. 26/2012 s. 62.

nodes.text:
If in a proceeding before the Supreme Court or the
County Court (the relevant sentencing court)—
despite anything to the contrary in this Division,
the proceeding for the offence under
section 83AC, 83AD, 83ADA or 83ADB may be
commenced by filing a charge-sheet in the
relevant sentencing court.

an offender is before the relevant sentencing
court and is convicted or found guilty of the
offence that is the subject of the proceeding;
and

the conviction or finding of guilt constitutes
a contravention of an order (the original
order) under this Act applying to the
offender, in respect of which a charge-sheet
may be filed for an offence under
section 83AC, 83AD, 83ADA or 83ADB;
and

the original order was made by the relevant
sentencing court—

If a charge-sheet is filed in the relevant sentencing
court under subsection (1) it must be filed by—
as the case requires.
the Director of Public Prosecutions; or

a crown prosecutor within the meaning of the
Criminal Procedure Act 2009; or

a member of staff of the Office of Public
Prosecutions who is a lawyer; or
a police officer; or

history.raw: S. 83AL(2)(d) amended by No. 37/2014 s. 10(Sch. item 151.3).

nodes.text:
an informant in the proceeding for which the
original order was made that is the subject of
the charge; or
a prescribed person; or
a member of a prescribed class of person; or
the Secretary—

The relevant sentencing court may hear and
determine the charge for the offence under
section 83AC, 83AD, 83ADA or 83ADB without
a jury and in accordance with Chapter 3 of the
Criminal Procedure Act 2009, subject to any
modifications as set out in the rules of the relevant
sentencing court.

nodes.heading: Process where offender before higher court, orders of Magistrates' Court

history.raw: S. 83AM inserted by No. 65/2011 s. 43, substituted by No. 26/2012 s. 62.

nodes.text:
If in a proceeding before the Supreme Court or the
County Court (the relevant sentencing court)—
despite anything to the contrary in this Division,
the relevant sentencing court may proceed to hear
and determine the proceeding for the offence
under section 83AC, 83AD, 83ADA or 83ADB as
if it were an unrelated summary offence within the
meaning of section 243 of the Criminal
Procedure Act 2009.

an offender is before the relevant sentencing
court and is convicted or found guilty of the
offence that is the subject of the proceeding;
and

the conviction or finding of guilt constitutes
a contravention of an order (the original
order) under this Act applying to the
offender, in respect of which a charge-sheet
may be filed for an offence under
section 83AC, 83AD, 83ADA or 83ADB;
and

the original order was made by the
Magistrates' Court—

Section 243 of the Criminal Procedure Act 2009
applies to the proceeding for the offence under
section 83AC, 83AD, 83ADA or 83ADB—

subject to any modifications as set out in the
rules of the relevant sentencing court; and
with any other necessary modifications.

nodes.heading: Powers of the court on finding of guilt for contravention of community correction order

nodes.text:
Subject to subsection (1A), if a court finds a
person guilty of an offence under section 83AD
(in addition to sentencing the offender for the
offence) the court must—

vary the order in any manner set out in
section 48M(2)(d), (e), (f), (g) or (h); or
confirm the order originally made; or

cancel the order (if it is still in force) and,
whether or not it is still in force, subject to
subsection (2), deal with the offender for the
offence with respect to which the order was
made in any manner in which the court could
deal with the offender as if it had just found
him or her guilty of that offence; or

cancel the order and make no further order
with respect to the offence with respect to
which the order was originally made.

If an offence under section 83AD is constituted
by a contravention of a mandatory treatment and
monitoring order—
subsection (1)(d) does not apply; and

if the court varies the mandatory treatment
and monitoring order, the order as varied
must be as onerous as, or more onerous than,
the order previously made; and

if the court cancels the mandatory treatment
and monitoring order, the court may impose
only—
a sentence of imprisonment; or

a mandatory treatment and monitoring
order that is as onerous as, or more
onerous than, the order previously
made; or

an order under subparagraph (ii) in
addition to a term of imprisonment
in accordance with section 44; or
a residential treatment order; or
a Court Secure Treatment Order.

A court, in determining how to deal with an
offender under subsection (1), must take into
account the extent to which the offender has
complied with the order.

The Secretary must disclose any direction he or
she has given under Division 3 of Part 3C to a
court making an assessment under subsection (2).

If the court finds a person guilty of an offence
under section 83AD in respect of a community
correction order and the person has paid a bond
under a bond condition of the community
correction order—
if the court makes an order under subsection

(a) or (b), the court may order that all or a
part of the bond is forfeited to the Crown; or
if the court makes an order under subsection

(c), the court must order that all or part of
the bond is forfeited to the Crown.

nodes.heading: Powers of court on finding of guilt for contravention of fines work order

history.raw: S. 83ASA inserted by No. 32/2013 s. 50 (as amended by No. 77/2013 s. 49).

nodes.text:
Subject to this section, if a court finds a person
guilty of an offence under section 83ADA
or 83ADB in relation to a fines work order,
(in addition to sentencing the offender for the
offence) the court must—
confirm the order or a part of the order; or
vary the order; or

cancel the order and deal with the offender
for the offence or offences with respect to
which the order was made in any manner in
which the court could deal with the offender
if it had just found him or her guilty of that
offence or those offences; or

cancel the order and make no further order
with respect to the offence or offences with
respect to which the order was originally
made.

Subsection (3) applies if the court is satisfied
that—

the circumstances of the offender have
materially altered since the fines work order
was made and as a result the offender is
unable to comply with the order; or

the circumstances of the offender were
wrongly stated or were not accurately
presented to the court before the fines work
order was made.

The court may make one or more of the following
orders—

discharge the outstanding fine or fines in
full; or

discharge up to two thirds of the outstanding
fine or fines; or

discharge up to two thirds of the outstanding
fine or fines and order that the offender be
imprisoned for a period of one day in respect
of each penalty unit, or part of a penalty unit,
to which the remaining undischarged amount
of the outstanding fine or fines is an
equivalent amount; or

adjourn the further hearing of the matter for
a period of up to 6 months.

If the court has made an order under
subsection (3)(b) or (c), the court may make an
order that the outstanding fines be paid by
instalments or an order that the offender be
allowed time to pay the outstanding fines.

Part 3B applies to an order under subsection (4) as
if it were an instalment order or a time to pay
order (as the case requires) made under that Part.

The court, in determining how to deal with an
offender under subsection (1) or (2), must take
into account the extent to which the offender has
complied with the order.

If the court considers that the orders that it may
make under subsection (1) or (3) are not adequate
because—
the court may impose a sentence of imprisonment
of 1 day for each penalty unit or part of a penalty
unit then remaining unpaid up to a maximum of
24 months.
of the nature of the offence; and
of the characteristics of the offender; and

the offender has intentionally refused to pay
the fine or instalment and to perform unpaid
community work—

nodes.heading: Powers of the court on finding of guilt for contravention of order for release on adjournment

nodes.text:
If in a proceeding for an offence under
section 83AC, the court finds the person guilty of
the offence the court must (in addition to
sentencing the offender for the offence)—

deal with the order under section 78, as if an
application had been made under that
section; or
confirm the order originally made; or

cancel the order (if it is still in force), and,
whether or not it is still in force, deal with
the offender for the offence with respect to
which the order was made in any manner in
which the court could deal with the offender
if it had just found him or her guilty of that
offence; or

make no further order with respect to the
offence in respect of which the original order
was made.

A court, in determining how to deal with an
offender under subsection (1), must take into
account the extent to which the offender has
complied with the order.

nodes.heading: Direction of certain conditions on failure to comply
Direction of unpaid community work condition on failure to comply

nodes.text:
If an offender fails to comply, without reasonable
excuse, with a community correction order that
has an unpaid community work condition
attached, the Secretary may direct the offender to
perform up to a maximum of 16 hours of unpaid
community work in a 12 month period in addition
to that imposed by the court that made the order.

The Secretary must not give a direction under
subsection (1) unless the Secretary is satisfied
that—

the failure to comply with the order is
sufficiently serious to give the direction; and

the failure to comply with the order is not
sufficiently serious to file a charge for the
offence under section 83AD; and

the unpaid community work condition has
not been completed; and

the number of hours of unpaid community
work that the offender is directed to perform
by the Secretary together with the number of
hours of unpaid community work that the
offender has been ordered to perform by the
court attaching the condition will not exceed
the maximum number of hours permitted
under section 48C(4).

nodes.heading: Direction of curfew condition on failure to comply

nodes.text:
If an offender fails to comply, without reasonable
excuse, with a community correction order that
has a curfew condition attached, the Secretary
may direct that the specified hours of each day
that the offender must remain at the place under
the condition be increased by up to 2 hours or that
the period that the condition applies to the order
be increased by up to 14 days in addition to that
imposed by the court that made the order.

The Secretary must not give a direction under
subsection (1) unless the Secretary is satisfied
that—

the failure to comply with the order is
sufficiently serious to give the direction; and

the failure to comply with the order is not
sufficiently serious to file a charge for the
offence under section 83AD; and
the curfew condition has not expired; and

the number of hours of each day that the
offender must remain at the place as directed
by the Secretary together with the number of
hours that the offender has been ordered to
remain at the place by the court attaching the
condition will not exceed the maximum
number of hours permitted under
section 48I(3); and

the period that the offender must remain at
the place under the curfew condition as
directed by the Secretary under
subsection (1) will not exceed the maximum
period under section 48I(3).

If the Secretary gives a direction under
subsection (1) and the offender is subject to an
electronic monitoring requirement attached to a
curfew condition under section 48LA the
Secretary must, if satisfied of the matters under
subsection (4), direct that the period that applies to
the requirement under section 48LA(5) or (6) is
increased by the same period specified in the
direction given under subsection (1).

The Secretary must not give a direction under
subsection (3) unless the Secretary is satisfied
that—

the electronic monitoring requirement that
the offender is subject to under section 48LA
has not expired; and

appropriate resources or facilities are
available to enable the offender to be
electronically monitored for the increased
period; and

the offender is a suitable person to be
electronically monitored for the increased
period; and

the increased period that the offender is to be
electronically monitored in respect of a
curfew condition does not exceed the
requirements of section 48I(3) for that
condition.

nodes.heading: Reasonable excuse for a failure to comply
nodes.text:
For the purposes of section 83AU or 83AV it is a
reasonable excuse for an offender to fail to
comply with a community correction order if—

there exists an application to vary the order
under section 48N relating to or resulting
from the failure to comply; or

the court varied the order under section 48M
in relation to or as a result of the failure to
comply.

nodes.heading: Notice of direction to be given in writing

nodes.text:
The Secretary must serve on an offender, by
ordinary service or personal service, notice in
writing of a decision under section 83AU
or 83AV.

In a notice under subsection (1) the Secretary
must include his or her reasons for making the
decision and the right of an offender to make an
application for review on the merits of the
Secretary's decision under section 83AY.

A decision of the Secretary under section 83AU
or 83AV does not take effect until the notice is
served under subsection (1) or any later date
specified in the notice.

In this section—
ordinary service has the same meaning as in the
Criminal Procedure Act 2009;
personal service has the same meaning as in the
Criminal Procedure Act 2009.

The court may review the decision of the
Secretary on application by the offender.

If the Secretary has given a direction in terms of
an unpaid community work condition or a curfew
condition under section 83AU or 83AV, the
offender may apply to the court that imposed the
condition for a review on the merits of the
Secretary's decision.

An application under subsection (2) must be made
within 28 days after the day on which the decision
was made.

The court may, on application of an offender,
extend the period within which an application
must be made under subsection (3).
A review under this section is a hearing de novo.

nodes.heading: Powers of a sentencing court on review

nodes.text:
In a review under section 83AY the court has the
same powers and duties that the Secretary has to
make the decision under this Division.

The Secretary must produce to the court the notice
served on the offender in accordance with
section 83AX.

In a review under section 83AY the court may, by
order—
confirm the decision under review; or
vary the decision under review; or
revoke the decision under review.

A decision of a court on a review is taken to have
effect from the time at which the court makes the
decision, unless the court orders otherwise.

nodes.heading: Purpose of Part
nodes.text:
The purpose of this Part is to enable a court to
make a superannuation order as a new sentencing
option where a person who is or has been a public
sector employee is convicted of an indictable
offence involving abuse of office, corruption or
perversion of the course of justice.

This Part applies in respect of an offender who is
convicted of a relevant offence on or after 3 June
2004 irrespective of whether the relevant offence
was committed before, on or after that date.

A court may make a superannuation order in
addition to, or instead of, any other sentence that
may be imposed under this or any other Act.

Despite sections 52, 53 and 55, the making of a
superannuation order under this Part is not to be
taken into account by a court in determining
whether to impose a fine on the offender under
section 49.
In this Part—

on the date of conviction on the amount
calculated under paragraph (a) of the
definition of residual employer financed

nodes.text:
means the
total sum, as determined by the

the amount (if any) of the

than as a public sector employee;
and
any relevant interest amount;

includes a reference to any corresponding
previous enactment and to any corresponding
subsequent enactment.
For the purposes of the definition of domestic

whether or not the information provided is

nodes.heading: Court may make a superannuation order

nodes.text:
If a court receives an application under
section 83E and is satisfied that section 83E(1)(a),
83E(1)(b) or 83E(1)(c) applies in respect of the
relevant offence, the court may make a
superannuation order if the court considers that
having regard, as far as is practicable, to the
matters specified in subsection (2) it is appropriate
to do so.
The matters are—

the financial circumstances of the offender,
including any other order that the court or
any other court has made or proposes to
make—

providing for the forfeiture of the
offender's property or the automatic
forfeiture of the offender's property by
operation of law; or

requiring the offender to make
restitution or pay compensation;

the nature of the burden that the making of
the superannuation order will impose and the
degree of hardship likely to result from the
making of the superannuation order on the
offender or his or her spouse, domestic
partner or dependants;

whether the administrators of a relevant
superannuation scheme have been served
with—

a superannuation agreement which
provides for a payment split; or

a flag lifting agreement which provides
for a payment split; or

a splitting order—
under Part VIIIB of the Family Law Act
1975 of the Commonwealth and the
non-member spouse's entitlements in respect
of the superannuation interest in the
superannuation benefit of the offender have
not been satisfied as at the relevant date;

the length of any period of membership of a
relevant superannuation scheme during
which the offender was not a public sector
employee;

the nature and gravity of the relevant
offence.

If the court imposes a superannuation order, the
court in determining the amount to be paid by the
offender under the superannuation order—

must have regard to the matters referred to in
subsection (2); and

must not determine an amount which
exceeds the total of the residual employer
financed components of the superannuation
benefits under the relevant superannuation
schemes.
A superannuation order takes effect—

at the end of the appeal period in respect of
the conviction for the relevant offence or the
sentence; or

if the offender appeals against the conviction
or sentence, subject to subsection (2), upon
the determination of the appeal.

If the conviction is set aside on appeal, the
superannuation order has no effect.

history.raw: S. 83G(2) amended by No. 68/2009 s. 97(Sch. item 110.61).

nodes.text:
If as the result of the determination of an appeal,
the court determining the appeal considers that the
superannuation order requires variation, the court
may vary the superannuation order.

A superannuation order varied under
subsection (3) takes effect as if it had been made
under section 83F.

nodes.heading: Provisions applying to a superannuation order
nodes.text:
Sections 56, 57, 58, 59, 60, 61, 64, 65, 69, 69A,
69B, 69C, 69E, 69F, 69H, 69K, 69L, 69M, 69N,
69O, 69P and 69ZB apply to and in respect of a
superannuation order as if the amount specified in
the superannuation order were a fine imposed
under section 49.

nodes.heading: Powers of an authorised person to require information

nodes.text:
If the authorised person proposes to make an
application in respect of an offender under
section 83E, the authorised person may request
the administrators of the relevant superannuation
scheme to provide any information that the
authorised person considers is necessary for the
purposes of making the application and which is
information the administrators have or ought to
have access to.

The administrators of the relevant superannuation
scheme must comply with a request under
subsection (1).
Penalty: 10 penalty units.

It is sufficient compliance with a request under
subsection (1) if the administrators of the relevant
superannuation scheme provide information in
response to the request and certify in writing that
they have used their best endeavours to provide
that information or are relying on the advice of, or
information provided by, a specified third party.

nodes.heading: Protection of administrators providing information
nodes.text:
The administrators of a relevant superannuation
scheme are not to be taken to be in breach of trust
or to have failed to comply with any provision of
the governing instrument of the superannuation
scheme only by virtue of complying with
section 83I.

nodes.heading: Disclosure of information
nodes.text:
Except to the extent necessary to comply with
section 83E, an authorised person or any person
employed or engaged by an authorised person
must not make any use of, or disclose to any
person, any information obtained under
section 83I.
Penalty: 5 penalty units.

history.raw: S. 84(4A)–(4C) inserted by No. 21/2020 s. 82, repealed by No. 35/2025 s. 90.

nodes.text:
If goods have been stolen and a person is found
guilty or convicted of an offence connected with
the theft (whether or not stealing is the gist of the
offence), the court may make—

an order that the offender deliver or transfer
to another person goods that directly or
indirectly represent the stolen goods (that is,
goods that are the proceeds of any disposal
or realisation of the whole or part of the
stolen goods or of goods so representing
them);

history.raw: S. 84(8)(b) substituted by No. 68/2009 s. 97(Sch. item 110.62).

nodes.text:
an order that a sum not exceeding the value
of the stolen goods be paid to another person
out of money taken from the offender's
possession on his or her arrest.

history.raw: S. 84(8)(c) repealed by No. 68/2009 s. 97(Sch. item 110.62).

nodes.text:
An order under paragraph (b) or (c) of
subsection (1) may only be made in favour of a
person who, if the stolen goods were in the
offender's possession, would be entitled to recover
them from him or her.

The court may make an order under both
paragraphs (b) and (c) of subsection (1) provided
that the person in whose favour the order is made
does not thereby recover more than the value of
the stolen goods.

If the court makes an order under paragraph (a) of
subsection (1) against a person and it appears to
the court that that person in good faith bought the
stolen goods from, or loaned money on the
security of the stolen goods to, the offender, the
court may, on the application of the purchaser or
lender, order that a sum not exceeding the
purchase price or the amount loaned (as the case
requires) be paid to the applicant out of money
taken from the offender's possession on his or her
arrest.
An order under this section—

may be made on an application made as soon
as practicable after the offender is found
guilty, or convicted, of the offence; and

may be made in favour of a person on an
application made—
by that person; or

on that person's behalf by the Director
of Public Prosecutions (if the
sentencing court was the Supreme
Court or the County Court) or the
informant or police prosecutor (if the
sentencing court was the Magistrates'
Court).

Nothing in subsection (5)(b)(ii) requires the
Director of Public Prosecutions or the informant
or police prosecutor (as the case requires) to make
an application on behalf of a person.

A court must not exercise the powers conferred by
this section unless in the opinion of the court the
relevant facts sufficiently appear from evidence
given at the hearing of the charge or from the
available documents, together with admissions
made by or on behalf of any person in connection
with the proposed exercise of the powers.

In subsection (7) the available documents
means—

any written statements or admissions which
were made for use, and would have been
admissible, as evidence on the hearing of the
charge; or
the depositions in the committal proceeding.
References in this section to—

stealing must be construed in accordance
with subsections (1) and (4) of section 90 of
the Crimes Act 1958; and
goods include references to a motor vehicle.

Subject to section 30 or section 36ZA of the
Confiscation Act 1997, an order made under
subsection (1)(c), (4), (4A) or (4B) of section 84
must be taken to be a judgment debt due by the
offender to the person in whose favour the order is
made and payment of any amount remaining
unpaid under the order may be enforced in the
court by which it was made.

An order made under section 84, other than an
order referred to in subsection (1), may be
enforced in the court by which it was made by any
means available to that court of enforcing an order
made by it in a civil proceeding.

nodes.heading: Compensation Subdivision (1)—Compensation for pain and suffering etc.

nodes.text: In this Subdivision—

history.raw: S. 85A(1) def. of sexual offence repealed by No. 47/2016 s. 41(2)(b).

nodes.heading: compensation order
nodes.text:
means an order under
section 85B(1);

nodes.heading: injury

nodes.text: actual physical bodily harm; or

mental illness or disorder or an
exacerbation of a mental illness or
disorder, whether or not flowing from
nervous shock; or
pregnancy; or

grief, distress or trauma or other
significant adverse effect; or

any combination of matters referred to
in paragraphs (a), (b), (c) and (d)
arising from an offence—

nodes.heading: medical expenses
nodes.text:
includes dental, optometry,
physiotherapy, psychology treatment,
hospital and ambulance expenses.

history.raw: S. 85A(1) def. of medical expenses amended by No. 47/2016 s. 41(2)(a).

nodes.text:
References in this Subdivision to the victim of an
offence must be construed having regard to the
definition of injury in subsection (1).

If a court—
it may, on the application of a person who has
suffered any injury as a direct result of the
offence, order the offender to pay compensation
of such amount as the court thinks fit for any
matter referred to in paragraphs (a) to (d) of
subsection (2).
finds a person guilty of an offence; or
convicts a person of an offence—

A compensation order may be made up of
amounts—

for pain and suffering experienced by the
victim as a direct result of the offence;

for some or all of any expenses actually
incurred, or reasonably likely to be incurred,
by the victim for reasonable counselling
services as a direct result of the offence;

for some or all of any medical expenses
actually and reasonably incurred, or
reasonably likely to be incurred, by the
victim as a direct result of the offence;

for some or all of any other expenses
actually and reasonably incurred, or
reasonably likely to be incurred, by the
victim as a direct result of the offence, not
including any expense arising from loss of or
damage to property.

In subsection (2) offence includes, in relation to a
person who has been found guilty or convicted of
an offence that was treated by the court as a
representative or sample charge, any other
occurrence of the same offence involved in the
course of conduct of which the charge was
representative or a sample.

history.raw: S. 85B(3) amended by No. 68/2009 s. 97(Sch. item 110.63).

nodes.text:
In making a compensation order the court may
direct that the compensation be paid by
instalments and that in default of payment of any
one instalment the whole of the compensation
remaining unpaid shall become due and payable.
An application for a compensation order—

must be made within 12 months after the
offender is found guilty, or convicted, of the
offence; and
may be made—
by the victim; or

on the victim's behalf by any person
other than the offender if the victim is a
child or is incapable of making the
application by reason of injury, disease,
senility, illness or physical or mental
impairment; or
on the victim's behalf—

if the sentencing court was a court
other than the Magistrates' Court,
by the Director of Public
Prosecutions; or

if the sentencing court was the
Magistrates' Court, by the Director
of Public Prosecutions, the
informant or police prosecutor.

Nothing in subsection (1)(b)(iii) requires the
Director of Public Prosecutions or the informant
or police prosecutor (as the case requires) to make
an application on behalf of a victim.

nodes.heading: Extension of time for making application

nodes.text:
A court may, on the application of a person who
wishes to apply for a compensation order, extend
the time within which an application for a
compensation order may be made if it is of the
opinion that it is in the interests of justice to do so.

A court may extend time under subsection (1)
before or after the time expires and whether or not
an application for an extension is made before the
time expires.

A court must not extend time under subsection (1)
without giving the offender a reasonable
opportunity to be heard on the matter.

In a proceeding on an application for a
compensation order a party—
may appear personally; or
may be represented by—
a legal practitioner; or

with the leave of the court, by any other
person.

A proceeding in a court on an application for a
compensation order made by or on behalf of a
child or other incapable person must be taken to
be a civil proceeding for the purpose of any
provision of an Act or rule of court relating to—
and any such provision applies in relation to a
proceeding on an application for a compensation
order with any necessary modifications.

the appointment or removal, and the power
or authority, of a litigation guardian in a civil
proceeding in that court; or

the administration of money ordered to be
paid to a child or such an incapable person—

nodes.heading: Court must not refuse to hear and determine application except in certain circumstances

nodes.text:
A court must not refuse to hear and determine an
application for a compensation order unless, in its
opinion, the relevant facts do not sufficiently
appear from—
together with admissions made by or on behalf of
any person in connection with the application.

evidence given at the hearing of the charge;
or

any statement of the material facts relevant
to the charge given to a court in a proceeding
for the offence by the prosecution and not
disputed by or on behalf of the accused; or

history.raw: S. 85F(1)(b) amended by No. 68/2009 s. 97(Sch. item 110.64).
S. 85F(2)(b) substituted by No. 68/2009 s. 97(Sch. item 110.65).

nodes.text: the available documents—

history.raw: S. 85F(2)(c) repealed by No. 68/2009 s. 97(Sch. item 110.65).

nodes.text:
In subsection (1)(c) the available documents
means—

any written statements or admissions which
were made for use, and would have been
admissible, as evidence on the hearing of the
charge; or

the depositions in the committal proceeding;
or

any victim impact statement made to the
court for the purpose of assisting it in
determining sentence, including any medical
report attached to it.
On an application for a compensation order—

the victim or the offender may give evidence
or may call another person to give evidence
in relation to the application; and

the victim, offender or other person who
gives evidence may be cross-examined and
re-examined; and

a finding of any fact made by a court in a
proceeding for the offence is evidence and,
in the absence of evidence to the contrary,
proof of that fact; and

the finding may be proved by production of a
document under the seal of the court from
which the finding appears; and

the court may have regard to any evidence or
statement referred to in section 85F(1) and,
with the consent of the parties to the
application, to any available documents or
admissions referred to in that section.

A court must not make a compensation order
without giving the offender a reasonable
opportunity to be heard on the application for the
order.

nodes.heading: Court may take financial circumstances of offender into account

nodes.text:
If a court decides to make a compensation order, it
may, in determining the amount and method of
payment of the compensation, take into account,
as far as practicable, the financial circumstances
of the offender and the nature of the burden that
its payment will impose.

A court is not prevented from making a
compensation order only because it has been
unable to find out the financial circumstances of
the offender.

nodes.heading: Court must reduce compensation by amount of assistance under victims of crime legislation
nodes.text:
If a court decides to make a compensation order, it
must reduce the amount of the compensation by
the amount of—
for the expense or other matter for which
compensation is being sought under this
Subdivision.

history.raw: S. 85I inserted by No. 54/2000 s. 21, substituted by No. 21/2022 s. 77.

nodes.text:
any award made to the victim under the
Victims of Crime Assistance Act 1996; or

any assistance paid to the victim under the
Victims of Crime (Financial Assistance
Scheme) Act 2022—

nodes.heading: Court to give reasons for its decision

nodes.text:
On deciding to grant or refuse an application for a
compensation order or to refuse to hear and
determine such an application, the court must—

state in writing the reasons for its decision;
and

cause those reasons to be entered in the
records of the court.

The failure of a court to comply with
subsection (1) does not invalidate the decision
made by it on the application.

nodes.heading: Costs of proceeding
nodes.text:
Despite any rule of law or practice to the contrary
or any provision to the contrary made by or under
any other Act, each party to a proceeding under
this Subdivision must bear their own costs of the
proceeding unless the court otherwise determines.

nodes.heading: Right to bring civil proceedings unaffected
nodes.text:
Nothing in this Subdivision takes away from, or
affects, the right of any person to recover damages
for any expense or other matter so far as it is not
satisfied by payment or recovery of compensation
under this Subdivision.

nodes.heading: Enforcement of order
nodes.text:
Subject to section 30 or section 36ZA of the
Confiscation Act 1997, a compensation order,
including costs ordered to be paid by the offender
on the proceeding for that order, must be taken to
be a judgment debt due by the offender to the
person in whose favour the order is made and
payment of any amount remaining unpaid under
the order may be enforced in the court by which it
was made.

history.raw: S. 85M inserted by No. 54/2000 s. 21, amended by No. 68/2010 s. 70(2).

nodes.heading: Subdivision (2)—Compensation for property loss
nodes.text: Subdivision (2)—Compensation for property loss

nodes.heading: Court to ask if application for compensation order will be made

nodes.text:
If a court finds a person guilty of, or convicts a
person of, an offence and evidence is presented in
a proceeding for the offence that loss or
destruction of, or damage to, property has
occurred as a result of the offence, the court must
ask the prosecution whether an application will be
made for a compensation order under section 86
in respect of the loss, destruction or damage.

To avoid doubt, a person is not prevented from
making an application for a compensation order
under section 86 merely because the court has not
taken the action referred to in subsection (1).

history.raw: S. 86(6A) inserted by No. 19/1999 s. 10, repealed by No. 54/2000 s. 22(2)(c).
S. 86(9A)–(9C) inserted by No. 81/1996 s. 74(2), repealed by No. 54/2000 s. 22(2)(e).

nodes.text:
If a court finds a person guilty of, or convicts a
person of, an offence it may order the offender to
pay to a person who has suffered loss or
destruction of, or damage to, property as a result
of the offence any compensation (not exceeding
the value of the property lost, destroyed or
damaged) that the court thinks fit.
An order under subsection (1) may be made—

on the application of a person suffering loss
or destruction of, or damage to, property as a
result of the offence; or

subject to subsection (1B)—on the court's
own motion.

history.raw: S. 86(9)(b) substituted by No. 68/2009 s. 97(Sch. item 110.66).

nodes.text:
A court may only make an order under
subsection (1) on its own motion if—

the court has given the offender the
opportunity to be heard in respect of the
order.

If a court decides to make an order under
subsection (1) it may in determining the amount
and method of payment of the compensation take
into account, as far as practicable, the financial
circumstances of the offender and the nature of
the burden that its payment will impose.

A court is not prevented from making an order
under subsection (1) only because it has been
unable to find out the financial circumstances of
the offender.

In making an order under subsection (1) the court
may direct that the compensation be paid by
instalments and that in default of payment of any
one instalment the whole of the compensation
remaining unpaid shall become due and payable.
An application under subsection (1A)(a)—

must be made as soon as practicable after the
offender is found guilty, or convicted, of the
offence; and
may be made—
by the person seeking compensation; or

on that person's behalf by the Director
of Public Prosecutions or (if the
sentencing court was the Magistrates'
Court) the informant or police
prosecutor.

Nothing in subsection (5)(b)(ii) requires the
Director of Public Prosecutions or the informant
or police prosecutor (as the case requires) to make
an application on behalf of a person.

In determining whether or not an order under
subsection (1) should be made and, if so, the
amount payable under the order—

a finding of any fact made by a court in a
proceeding for the offence is evidence and,
in the absence of evidence to the contrary,
proof of that fact; and

the finding may be proved by production of a
document under the seal of the court from
which the finding appears.

A court must not exercise the powers conferred by
this section unless in the opinion of the court the
relevant facts sufficiently appear from evidence
given at the hearing of the charge or from the
available documents, together with admissions
made by or on behalf of any person in connection
with the proposed exercise of the powers.

In subsection (8) the available documents
means—

history.raw: S. 86(9)(c) amended by No. 19/1999 s. 11, repealed by No. 68/2009 s. 97(Sch. item 110.66).

nodes.text:
any written statements or admissions which
were made for use, and would have been
admissible, as evidence on the hearing of the
charge; or

the depositions in the committal proceeding;
or

any victim impact statement made to the
court for the purpose of assisting it in
determining sentence; or

any other documentary evidence acceptable
to the court of—

loss or destruction of, or damage to,
property suffered by a person as a result
of the offence; or

the amount of the loss suffered or the
expense incurred as a result of that
destruction or damage.

Despite any rule of law or practice to the contrary
or any provision to the contrary made by or under
any other Act, each party to a proceeding under
this section must bear their own costs of the
proceeding unless the court otherwise determines.

Nothing in this section takes away from, or affects
the right of, any person to recover damages for, or
to be indemnified against, any loss, destruction or
damage so far as it is not satisfied by payment or
recovery of compensation under this section.

References in this section to property include
references to a motor vehicle.

nodes.heading: Enforcement of compensation order
nodes.text:
Subject to section 30 or section 36ZA of the
Confiscation Act 1997, an order under
section 86(1), including costs ordered to be paid
by the offender on the proceeding for that order,
must be taken to be a judgment debt due by the
offender to the person in whose favour the order is
made and payment of any amount remaining
unpaid under the order may be enforced in the
court by which it was made.

nodes.heading: Recovery of assistance paid under victims of crime legislation
